# Research claims and estimation

A source preserves reference, title/type, publication date, applicable date, location/excerpt, reliability, and demo/live status. A claim preserves a stable ID, normalized metric/value/unit, extraction confidence, conflict links, and whether the model uses it. Bundled claims demonstrate collection → extraction → normalization → conflict review → preferred value → assumption mapping → gap detection → estimate proposal → human approval.

Estimates remain distinct from reported facts. Supported demo methods are peer range, historical relationship, pipeline conversion, margin bridge, and funding/headcount triangulation. Each estimated node exposes rationale, method, evidence, confidence, low/base/high range, creation date, and prior value. Research priority multiplies normalized outcome impact, uncertainty, evidence weakness, and practical verifiability. It is a planning heuristic, not a probability or Bayesian analysis.
